title: Global allocator default-method selection, initialization, and shutdown

scope.rationale: These three functions select the pinned default mem1 backend, initialize allocator mutex/backend/page-cache configuration, clear mem0 on failure, and shut down/reset allocator state. They are the immediate lifecycle closure required before the global allocation core.
excluded_responsibilities: Top-level sqlite3_initialize/sqlite3_shutdown reference counting and recursion
Page-cache subsystem initialization beyond allocator-time pPage validation
Non-mem1 allocator backends from other build profiles

external_source_responsibilities: Exact public sqlite3_mem_methods ABI-to-Backend configuration transport
dependencies.caller_closure: Default backend selection and direct allocator init/end are assigned. Top-level lifecycle is assigned but scaffolded; static page-cache consumer and final memory-method configuration integration remain blocking.

inputs: Pre-initialization configured allocator methods and static page-cache settings
outputs: Initialized allocator backend and mutex, or exact initialization result with mem0 cleared
contracts.ownership: Configured method context remains caller-owned. Allocator owns its mutex/state lifecycle and invokes xShutdown only after successful startup.
contracts.state_and_results: Missing xMalloc selects mem1 defaults. Invalid static page-cache settings are zeroed. xInit result is returned; failure zeroes mem0. End invokes xShutdown if present then clears mem0.
contracts.locks_callbacks_io: Allocates STATIC_MEM mutex and invokes configured xInit/xShutdown callbacks. No I/O.
contracts.failure_and_continuation: Failed xInit leaves allocator-local limits/nearly-full/start state cleared and permits later reconfiguration/retry.

representation_differences: Manager is constructed with systemBackend, so C nullable xMalloc/default-method selection is represented by a non-null default backend value.
Manager receives the shared process STATIC_MEM identity at start and clears its nullable mem0 mutex reference on initialization failure and shutdown.
Manager resets allocator-local limits/nearly-full state on init failure and shutdown and now preserves source static page-cache validation before xInit.

oracle.protocol: Infrastructure C/Zig differential compares default/configured backend initialization and shutdown counts, method-table copy behavior, repeated/shuffled lifecycle, allocation after init, and shutdown idempotence. Native tests inject backend init failure and verify allocator-local state clearing.
oracle.normalization: Embedded versus allocated STATIC_MEM mutex address is ignored; callback sequence, results, and allocator state are exact.

assurance.oom: Injected initialization failure clears allocator-local state; mutex-allocation OOM integration remains open.
assurance.io_crash_concurrency: No I/O. Top-level concurrent initialization and mutex lifecycle remain blocking.
assurance.malformed_input: Null storage, sub-512 page size, and nonpositive page count clear pPage/szPage exactly; broader backend configuration validation remains open.
assurance.continuation: Failure retry and repeated stop are tested natively; full sqlite3_initialize continuation is external.
assurance.performance: Direct backend callbacks; final mutex allocation topology remains open.

integration.native_call_path: global.process_coordinator exclusively starts/stops memory.process_manager; public APIs initialize through that coordinator and internal allocation paths use memory.processManager only after startup.
integration.bounded_owner_retired: Yes for production allocator lifecycle: the memory-only lazy-start and direct shutdown helpers were removed, and verify-config rejects their return. Final typed configuration and top-level lifecycle trace promotion remain separate dependencies.

independent_review.notes: Internal lifecycle traces pass; integration with final typed configuration/top-level lifecycle, assurance, and independent review remain.

known_blockers: Top-level sqlite3_initialize/shutdown now has exclusive production ownership, but its source-equivalent refcount/condition event trace and final typed memory-configuration API remain integration work.
Static page-cache configuration validation is trace-equivalent here, but the page-cache subsystem must consume the same configured owner before integration.

implementation_spans: upstream/sqlite/src/malloc.c:150-194 was reviewed completely for sqlite3MallocInit/sqlite3MallocEnd and adjacent pressure-state ownership
upstream/sqlite/src/mem1.c:240-293 was reviewed for system allocator shutdown and the complete default sqlite3_mem_methods table installed by sqlite3MemSetDefault
upstream/sqlite/src/main.c:225-255 and 380-414 were reviewed for top-level start/partial-layer/shutdown ordering
src/core/memory.zig Manager.start/stop and systemBackend are canonical AST-hashed targets
callers: sqlite3_initialize invokes sqlite3MallocInit after mutex initialization and marks isMallocInit only on success
sqlite3_shutdown calls sqlite3MallocEnd after PCache shutdown and before mutex shutdown, including partial initialized state
sqlite3MemSetDefault is selected only when xMalloc is null; sqlite3_config owns method-table copying/validation outside this unit
callees: sqlite3MallocInit selects mem1 defaults, borrows STATIC_MEM, validates pPage/szPage/nPage, invokes xInit(pAppData), and zeroes mem0 on failure
sqlite3MallocEnd conditionally invokes xShutdown(pAppData) and always zeroes mem0
mem1 default table binds malloc/free/realloc/size/roundup/init/shutdown and null context
assertions_branches_cleanup: Five behavior IDs cover absent-backend selection, invalid static page settings, failed xInit clearing, result return, and optional xShutdown
Invalid static page configuration clears pPage and szPage but source leaves nPage unchanged
Failed init owns no started mem0 state and permits retry; successful shutdown callback precedes local state clearing
No file I/O occurs; callback-owned resources remain callback responsibility
upstream_tests: upstream/sqlite/test/malloc.test family and memsubsys1.test/memsubsys2.test exercise allocator configuration, limits, lifecycle, faults, and status
upstream/sqlite/test/mutex2.test exercises initialization failures and continuation across subsystem boundaries
Project memory/global tests and infrastructure differential cover configured/default callbacks, invalid static page settings, failure clearing, cycles, and retry; receipts remain later
